title: The Use of the Ex Vivo Chandler Loop Apparatus to Assess the Biocompatibility of Modified Polymeric Blood Conduits
protocol: Prepare a solution of PDT-BzPh at 1 mg/ml and potassium bicarbonate at 0.7 mg/ml in sterile water.
Stir the prepared solution overnight at 4 °C, protected from light.
Cut polymeric tubing into 40 cm long pieces.
Soak the tubes in a 0.1% aqueous hexacylpyridinium solution for 90 min at room temperature on a shaker or Chandler Loop Apparatus.
Rinse the tubes with sterile water three times after soaking.
Acidify the PDT-BzPh solution by adding 50 µl of 15% potassium phosphate monobasic (KH2PO4) per ml of PDT-BzPh to form a cloudy micellar solution.
Soak the tubes in the acidified PDT-BzPh solution for 40 min at room temperature on a shaker or apparatus.
Rinse the tubes once with dilute acetic acid (1:1,000).
Expose the tubes to UV irradiation for 60 min total duration, rotating the tubes one-quarter turn every 15 minutes.
Soak the tubes in a potassium bicarbonate solution at 20 mg/ml for 20 min at room temperature on a shaker or apparatus.
Rinse the tubes with sterile water three times and store them at 4 °C in sterile water.
Dissolve 5 mg of Sulfo-SMCC in 200 µl of Dimethylformamide (DMF).
Add 50 µl of Sulfo-SMCC solution to a 0.1 mg/ml recCD47 poly-lysine solution.
Stir the mixture for 60 min at room temperature.
Degas sterile Dulbecco’s Phosphate Buffered Saline (DPBS).
Purify Sulfo-SMCC reacted recCD47 using a 7K molecular weight cut-off spin desalting column according to manufacturer's instructions.
Collect the final flow-through of purified recCD47.
Dilute the collected solution with DPBS to coat the interior of the tube.
Rinse tubes from day 2 with sterile, degassed DPBS three times.
React the modified surface of the tubes with a solution of 20 mg/ml TCEP in degassed DPBS for less than 2 min.
Rinse the tubes with sterile degassed DPBS four times.
Add Sulfo-SMCC-reacted recCD47 to the tubes and incubate overnight at 4 °C on a shaker or apparatus.
Rinse modified tubes to be quantified from day 3 with DPBS three times.
Store unused tubes in DPBS at 4 °C.
Use a 4 mm biopsy punch to make duplicate tube samples for each test sample.
Place the biopsy punches in wells of a 96-well plate.
Prepare a negative control using an unmodified tube without detection antibody treatment.
Prepare an antibody control using an unmodified tube treated with the detection antibody.
Prepare modified tubing test samples treated with the detection antibody.
Block samples with 0.4% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in DPBS for 60 min at room temperature on a shaker.
Aspirate BSA and rinse with tris-buffered saline plus 1% Tween-20 (TBST) 3x, 10 min each on a shaker.
Prepare a working dilution of antibody in 0.4% BSA according to manufacturer’s recommended dilution for immunoassays.
Dilute human CD47 Antibody B6H12-FITC 1:100 in 0.4% BSA.
Add 200 μl of antibody dilution to appropriate wells.
Incubate negative controls with 0.4% BSA only.
Incubate at room temperature for 60 min on a shaker (protect from light).
Rinse with TBST 3x, 10 min each on a shaker.
Aspirate the last TBST rinse and add 200 μl DPBS to tube sample wells.
Collect the final flow-through, which is high-quality thiol-reactive recombinant CD47.
Dilute recCD47 to coat the interior of the tubes with DPBS.
Read FITC signal intensity using a microplate reader with FITC excitation (485 nm) and emission (538 nm) settings.
Fill water bath with distilled water until approximately half of the diameter wheels are submerged.
Add enough bleach to the water bath to make a 10% bleach solution.
Set water bath temperature to 37 °C and allow it to equilibrate.
Assemble metal adapters, unmodified tubing, and modified tubing around apparatus wheels.
Fit tubing snuggly around the wheel with the metal adapter in place.
Obtain 30 ml blood sample using an IRB-approved protocol in a vial prefilled with 2 ml of citrate or other anticoagulant.
Mix blood by inversion to prevent clotting once collected.
Add approximately 10 ml of blood to each tube using the metal valve and syringe, leaving some air in the tube.
Secure the valve cap and rotate for 3 hr.
Drain the blood into a waste beaker treated with a 10% bleach solution or as required by institutional policy.
Gently rinse tubing interior with DPBS to remove all traces of blood.
Collect flow-through in the waste beaker.
Dispose of blood in accordance with institutional policy.
Disinfect the apparatus and any blood contacting surfaces using a 10% bleach solution or according to institutional policy.
Prepare a 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution.
Incubate tubing in a 4% PFA solution overnight at 4 °C.
Remove 4% PFA after overnight incubation.
Rinse films very gently with DPBS.
Cut the tubing into sections to expose the lumen surface for staining.
Stain a section of the tubing with mounting media containing DAPI for 30 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Rinse the tubing very gently with DPBS after staining to reduce background DAPI signal.
Image the stained tubing using a fluorescent microscope equipped with a DAPI filter and digital camera under 200X magnification.
Count the number of cells in 9 blindly selected fields of view.
Record cell counts per field of view.
Perform appropriate statistical analyses to determine statistical significance of results.
Prepare a 2% glutaraldehyde solution (Caution: Perform in fume hood).
Incubate tubing in a 2% glutaraldehyde solution overnight at 4 °C.
Gently rinse the tubing with DPBS three times after overnight incubation.
Prepare a 1% osmium tetroxide solution (Caution: Severe inhalation hazard! Use in fume hood).
Incubate tubing in a 1% osmium tetroxide solution for 15 min at room temperature.
Gently rinse the tubing with DPBS three times after incubation.
Prepare a series of ethanol concentrations (25%, 50%, 75%, 95%, and 100%).
Dehydrate the tubing by incubating in each ethanol concentration as follows: 25%, 50%, 75%, and 95% for 20 min each; then 100% for 30 min.
Supercritical point dry the tubing with CO2 for 45 min to remove all moisture.
Mount tube sections on a specimen stub with silver paste or graphite.
Coat tube sections with 12.5 nm of gold-palladium.
Examine in a scanning electron microscope.
